builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
summary: It replaces direct VLM solving and visual chain-of-thought (e.g., Canvas-CoT) with an inference-time harness that registers physical scopes, constructs derived views, and invalidates dependent claims on revision, without weight updates. Cost is extra inference calls, generated derived views, and bookkeeping of a scope-aware working memory, increasing latency and orchestration complexity while remaining API-compatible. It can fail when proposed revisions or scope links are themselves wrong, when dependent invalidation is incomplete, and the reported gains may not transfer beyond physics-diagram reasoning.
rationale: The method is feasible with third-party multimodal APIs and no training, but its quantified benefit is benchmark- and domain-specific, so adoption should follow validation on the reader's own workloads.

claims.statement: It replaces direct VLM solving and visual chain-of-thought (e.g., Canvas-CoT) with an inference-time harness that registers physical scopes, constructs derived views, and invalidates dependent claims on revision, without weight updates. Cost is extra inference calls, generated derived views, and bookkeeping of a scope-aware working memory, increasing latency and orchestration complexity while remaining API-compatible. It can fail when proposed revisions or scope links are themselves wrong, when dependent invalidation is incomplete, and the reported gains may not transfer beyond physics-diagram reasoning.
On PhysAlign it exceeds direct solving across all six evaluated VLMs; with Gemini-3.8-flash it surpasses Canvas-CoT by 9.34 percentage points and improves OOD solving accuracy on PhysUniBench.
